summary_sentence: Google I/O launched Gemini 3.5 Flash + Spark; coverage split between insider podcasts (DeepMind's Logan Kilpatrick + Tulsee Doshi on Cognitive Revolution) and skeptical takes (Theo's 187k 'scared to make this video' opener, plus his follow-up framing Codium's Composer 2.5 as the more impressive recent small-code-model drop).
praises: four times faster than other leading frontier models per the explainer breakdowns
shipped alongside a new Frontier Safety Framework and interpretability tools that inspect reasoning before output
DeepMind framing positions 3.5 Flash + Antigravity 2.0 + Spark as a single connected agentic stack rather than three separate products
complaints: Theo's 187k YouTube reaction opens with explicit fear of Google retaliation, citing the Anti-Gravity demonetization precedent
AI Daily Brief calls Google's broader AI strategy 'getting messier and messier' even while crediting the speed advantage
Theo's 118k follow-up positions Codium Composer 2.5 as the small-and-effective code model Gemini 3.5 Flash 'should have been'

notable_quotes.author: @Theo - t3.gg
notable_quotes.quote: I'm scared to make this video. Google just dropped Gemini 3.5 Flash. It's definitely a model.

notable_quotes.author: @AI Daily Brief
notable_quotes.quote: Their AI strategy is getting messier and messier, but it also just might not matter.

notable_quotes.author: @kanekallaway
notable_quotes.quote: Gemini 3.5 Flash is Google's latest AI model that has frontier level capabilities, but is also four times faster than all the other leading models.

podcast_synth.synth_line: Theo opens with explicit fear of Google retaliation (Anti-Gravity demonetization precedent) before delivering his Gemini 3.5 Flash critique.
Theo argues Codium's Composer 2.5 is the small-but-effective code model Gemini 3.5 Flash should have been, framing Google as a step behind a smaller competitor.
DeepMind's Logan Kilpatrick and Tulsee Doshi defend the 3.5 Flash + Omni + Spark slate as a connected agentic stack in the show's first-ever in-person episode.
Kevin Roose and Casey Newton break down the I/O slate (Gemini 3.5, Spark, Omni) against the question of whether Google is doing enough to win the AI race.
AI Daily Brief calls Google's I/O strategy 'messier and messier' while acknowledging Gemini 3.5 Flash's speed advantages might matter regardless.

creator_recommendation.angle: Side-by-side: run the same agentic code workflow through Gemini 3.5 Flash + Antigravity 2.0 and Codium's Composer 2.5; settle Theo's 'should have been Gemini' claim with shipped output, not vibes.
creator_recommendation.hook: Theo says Codium's Composer 2.5 is the model Gemini 3.5 Flash should have been. I gave both eight hours on the same Next.js feature. Here is what they actually built.
